item.title: Nvidia’s Show of Financial Force Soothes Jittery Credit Markets
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s commitments to backstop the artificial intelligence boom seemed to be swelling by the day. There was the reported $250 billion to help kickstart a massive data center for OpenAI in Ohio, the latest in a string of big financings it was involved with.

item.title: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3: A New Contender in the US-China AI Race: Podcast
item.description: Chinese startup Moonshot has put the AI world on notice. On today’s Big Take Asia podcast: What Kimi K3 means for the future of the global race for AI supremacy.

item.title: CoreWeave Revenue Surges on Booming Demand for AI Computing
item.description: CoreWeave Inc., a provider of computing that powers artificial intelligence systems, topped analysts’ estimates for second-quarter sales after signing up more customers in a booming market.

item.title: Super Micro Gives Sales Forecast That Tops Rosiest Projections
item.description: Super Micro Computer Inc. gave a sales forecast for the current quarter that topped analysts’ estimates, a sign the booming artificial intelligence market continues to bolster sales of the company’s servers.

item.title: Former Hedge Fund CFO Pleads Guilty to Embezzling $3 Million
item.description: The former chief financial officer of a Miami Beach hedge fund admitted he embezzled more than $3 million over four years at the firm, approving phony invoices and using corporate credit cards for adult entertainment and personal travel.

item.title: Nvidia Can’t Solve the Two Big AI Buildout Problems
item.description: Scarcity and profit margin.

item.title: Omers Returns 4.8% in 2026, Fueled by Stocks and US Dollar
item.description: Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System returned 4.8% in the first half of the year, gaining C$6.9 billion ($5 billion) from a strong US dollar and rising stock market.

item.title: Nigeria Boosts Tax Breaks to Lure $50 Billion in Deepwater Oil
item.description: Nigeria is offering sweeping tax incentives to attract as much as $50 billion into deepwater oil and gas projects and revive capital-intensive developments that have stalled for decades.

item.title: Colombia Coffee Exports Largely Halted After Deadly Earthquake
item.description: Colombian coffee exports are largely paused after a devastating earthquake disrupted operations at the nation’s main port and triggered roadblocks along key highways, according to the head of a coffee exporters’ group.

item.title: French Economy Set to Maintain Momentum, Central Bank Says
item.description: France’s economy is set to maintain its momentum this quarter, thanks to growth in key sectors and cooler inflation, according to the central bank.

item.title: RUM Group Sees Path to 30-Fold Revenue Gain on AI Power Capacity
item.description: RUM Group Inc. Chief Executive Chris Pavlovski said the company’s 250 megawatts of currently unmonetized power capacity represents a potential 30-fold sales boost in the wake of its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Apple Executive in Charge of Apple Pay and Wallet Services Is Leaving
item.description: Apple Inc.’s Jennifer Bailey, the longtime head of Pay and Wallet services, is retiring after more than two decades at the company, adding to a sweeping changing of the guard at the iPhone maker.

item.title: US-Japan Intervention Sets Stage for a Yen Rally, Eurizon Says
item.description: The US and Japanese effort to prop up the yen is “a watershed moment” that will keep it from sliding back to its four-decade low against the dollar, according to Eurizon SLJ Capital’s Stephen Jen.

item.title: Colombia to Declare Economic Emergency to Bolster Quake Relief
item.description: Colombia’s government plans to declare an economic emergency to bolster its response to a massive earthquake, Finance Minister Miguel Gómez told lawmakers on Tuesday.

item.title: Texas Power Demand Forecast Trimmed After Data Center Pause
item.description: Demand for electricity in Texas is expected to grow at a far slower pace after the state imposed a pause on new data center projects.

item.title: Citadel Securities Says Prepare for a Reload on Levered Stock Bets
item.description: Systematic buyers are getting ready to load up on stocks again after a massive unwind, according to Citadel Securities.

item.title: Hawaii Taps Muni Market to Finish First US Driverless Rail Line
item.description: Hawaii’s capital is trading surfboards for light-rail trains as it bets on a new way to get around.

item.title: US Sees Iran War Oil Supply Disruptions Lasting Through 2027
item.description: The US now expects oil supply disruptions stemming from the US-Iran war to reach about 600,000 barrels per day through the end of next year as the conflict continues to crimp shipments via the critical Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Uber Exits Serve Robotics Stake as Delivery Alliance Unravels
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. has divested from long-time partner Serve Robotics Inc. as the two companies clash over how to deploy delivery robots, the latest setback in Uber’s push to facilitate autonomous services on its platform.

item.title: SpaceXAI Unveils Grok Bot to Work Like a Team of AI Agents
item.description: SpaceXAI is rolling out new artificial intelligence software that’s designed to act like a team of AI agents fielding assignments throughout the day, marking the latest bid by Elon Musk’s company to keep pace with Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

item.title: Chile Cuts Copper Production Forecast Again as Mine Woes Persist
item.description: Chile lowered its copper production forecast for a second straight quarter as weaker output from some of the country’s biggest mines adds to supply constraints that have helped push up prices.

item.title: Sonos Plans ‘Ace Ultra’ Headphones and Broad Push Into AI
item.description: Sonos Inc. is readying a new pair of wireless headphones, the first product in an upcoming hardware wave that will see the audio company push deeper into artificial intelligence and frame its signature whole-home system as an ideal match for cutting-edge AI models and voice interactions.

item.title: AI Data Center Boom Is ‘Maxing Out’ P&C Insurers, AIG CEO Says
item.description: American International Group Inc. Chief Executive Officer Eric Andersen said that while the artificial intelligence buildout presents a “great opportunity” for the insurance industry, it’s also pushing property and casualty providers to their limits.

item.title: Barclays Sees Picky Bond Buyers Keeping Yields at Multiyear Peak
item.description: A shift in the buyer base of US Treasuries toward value-oriented mutual funds, households and other private investors has helped propel 30-year yields to multi-decade peaks, according to Barclays Plc.

item.title: OpenAI Executive Brad Lightcap Leaves to ‘Start Something New’
item.description: OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap is leaving the artificial intelligence company to start a new project, months after he stepped away from his role as chief operating officer.

item.title: SEC Weighs Direct Funding for Costly Market-Tracking Database
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission is considering taking direct control of a controversial database that tracks trades across US equities and options markets after Citadel Securities won a lawsuit challenging its funding last year.

item.title: A Solar Eclipse Will Flip the Off Switch on Europe’s Solar Farms
item.description: Night will fall on Europe’s power system a bit early Wednesday evening, as an eclipse is set to block solar generation across parts of the UK and western Europe.

item.title: Radiant World Offers $150 Million Aluminum Stash for Sale
item.description: Metals trader Radiant World has been seeking to sell a stockpile of aluminum worth some $150 million at a small discount to market prices in an attempt to boost its liquidity, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nvidia Credit Risk Eases After CEO Clarifies $500 Billion Plan
item.description: Bond traders dialed back measures of credit risk associated with Nvidia Corp. on Tuesday after the company said it would limit its exposure in a $500 billion plan to finance the type of artificial-intelligence investments that are driving demand for its computer chips.

item.title: JBS Seeks US Margin Recovery With New CEO Pledging Continuity
item.description: JBS NV said its main business of US beef is yet to benefit from a restructuring plan, but sees that effort as well as a renewed flow of Mexican cattle eventually aiding meatpacking margins.
